staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable worktree. The saved ASan stack matches `encoding.c:539`, `readclause.c:174`, and `readclause.c:798` in this snapshot, and `patch.diff` adds `!Eof()` to the vulnerable `ReadClause()` punctuation-run loops at current lines 780 and 797.

bug_description.original: AddressSanitizer reported a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in `string_decoder_getc_utf_8`, reached through `text_decoder_getc` and `GetC`, while `ssml-fuzzer` parsed attacker-controlled input in espeak-ng.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness is the exact two-byte file `2e 2e` (`..`). The harness appends one NUL byte and passes that heap buffer into synchronous `espeak_Synth()`, but `espeak_ng_Synthesize()` ignores the explicit size and `text_decoder_decode_string()` recomputes the decoder length as `strlen(string) + 1`, initializing `p_decoder` over the three-byte range `..\0`. `ReadClause()` then reads the two dots, uses its repeated-dot probe to consume the appended NUL in-bounds, and leaves `p_decoder.current == p_decoder.end` while `c2` still holds the second `'.'`. A later punctuation-run scan uses composite clause-bit tests that still evaluate true for `.` and, because that loop lacks the patch's `!Eof()` guard, it calls `GetC()` at EOF. The UTF-8 backend finally dereferences `*decoder->current++` one byte past the 3-byte heap buffer, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input state. The synchronous text decoder ignores the harness `size` and recomputes the attacker-controlled string length from the NUL-terminated witness buffer itself.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has SHA-256 `5ec1f7e700f37c3d0b2981d04855fc34b94aaa15457b05ca571817442d228f81` and exact bytes `2e 2e` (`..`). `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c` copies those bytes into `str`, appends `0x00`, and calls `espeak_Synth(..., size + 1, ...)`; in synchronous mode `espeak_ng_Synthesize()` marks `size` unused at `speech.c:665`, so `text_decoder_decode_string()` measures the resulting `..\0` string with `strlen(string) + 1`.

sink.description: ASan sink. After `ReadClause()` has already advanced the decoder to EOF, the UTF-8 backend dereferences `decoder->current` at `decoder->end` and reads one byte past the heap-backed witness string.
sink.note: The saved ASan report records `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/libespeak-ng/encoding.c:539:15`, with the faulting address `0x602000000153` located `0` bytes to the right of the 3-byte `..\0` heap region allocated by `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c`.

root_cause.description: Missing EOF guard on the punctuation-run scan. Once `c2` still holds `'.'` and the decoder has already reached EOF, this loop still stays true and permits another `GetC()` from the exhausted buffer.
root_cause.note: The staged patch repairs this exact obligation by changing the loop header to `while(!Eof() && clause_type_from_codepoint(c2) & (CLAUSE_QUESTION | CLAUSE_EXCLAMATION)) {`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness materializes the exact two-byte witness as a heap string, appends one NUL terminator, and submits the resulting three-byte UTF-8 buffer to espeak-ng with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`.

parser_admitted.description: Synchronous synthesis hands the heap-backed witness into the project text decoder before `SpeakNextClause()` and `TranslateClause()` begin clause parsing.

coarse_trace.summary: The decoder derives `length = strlen(string) + 1` from the attacker-controlled `..\0` buffer and initializes the UTF-8 decoder range over those three bytes.
The clause reader consumes both dots, then its repeated-dot probe consumes the appended NUL in-bounds and leaves `p_decoder.current == p_decoder.end` while `c2` still equals `'.'`.
Composite clause-bit tests treat `.` as matching the question/exclamation punctuation scan, and the missing `!Eof()` guard lets that loop issue another `GetC()` at EOF.
The EOF-time `GetC()` reaches the UTF-8 backend, which dereferences one byte past the 3-byte heap buffer and triggers the saved ASan read overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. `text_decoder_decode_string_multibyte()` reaches this helper with `length < 0`, so synchronous synthesis measures the attacker-controlled NUL-terminated witness itself. For the saved `..\0` string, `length` becomes `3`.

The helper selects the UTF-8 getter and initializes the decoder over the exact three-byte range `[string, string + 3)`: first dot, second dot, appended NUL. Later EOF checks compare `decoder->current` against this `decoder->end` pointer.
`ReadClause()` fetches the first byte from `p_decoder` into lookahead `c2`. On the witness this returns the first `'.'` and advances `decoder->current` to the second byte.
At the top of the loop, the first dot stored in `c2` becomes the current punctuation character `c1`.
`GetC()` reads the second `'.'` into lookahead `c2`. `Eof()` is still false immediately afterward, so the appended NUL remains the next unread decoder byte.

The repeated-dot probe tests for a third dot. For the exact `..\0` witness, its `GetC()` consumes the in-bounds NUL, returns `0`, never enters the loop body, and `UngetC(0)` leaves nothing queued back; `p_decoder.current` is now equal to `p_decoder.end` while `c1` and `c2` still hold the two dots.
The first dot is classified as `CLAUSE_PERIOD`. That value is a composite clause bitfield, not a dedicated one-bit tag.

This guard is still true for `CLAUSE_PERIOD`, because `CLAUSE_QUESTION` and `CLAUSE_EXCLAMATION` are composite constants that share the sentence and pause bits present in `CLAUSE_PERIOD`. Control therefore enters the punctuation-run scan even though the current character is `'.'`.

Root-cause step. `c2` is still the second `'.'`, so the same composite-bit test keeps the loop header true. Because the header lacks the patch's `!Eof()` check, the loop proceeds even though step 6 already left `p_decoder.current == p_decoder.end`.
The loop body now calls `GetC()` at EOF. The saved ASan stack records this exact caller site (`ReadClause:798`) flowing into `GetC:174` and `text_decoder_getc:769` with the exhausted decoder state.

Sink. Because step 10 reaches the UTF-8 backend with `decoder->current == decoder->end`, this dereference reads one byte past the 3-byte `..\0` heap buffer, exactly as reported by the saved ASan trace.

format.name: raw-utf8-ssml-input
format.contract: The witness is the exact two-byte UTF-8 file `2e 2e` (`..`). The harness appends one NUL byte and synchronous espeak-ng remeasures that string as `..\0`; `ReadClause()` then consumes the terminator in the repeated-dot probe and the later punctuation-run loop without `!Eof()` issues the crashing `GetC()` from EOF. This GT is grounded only for that exact witness and the saved reproduction.
